full_text_en:
Dayang Company v. Huanghe Company — dispute over patent implementation license contract

【Ruling Summary】

After a patent technology implementation license contract takes effect, if the patent technology licensor, in accordance with the contract, provides the patent technology licensee with specialized production equipment containing the patented technology for the purpose of enabling the licensee to produce and sell patented products, this does not constitute the circumstance of "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress" as stipulated in Article 329 of the Contract Law of the PRC.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min San Zhong Zi No. 8

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd., domiciled at Zengcuoan, Siming District, Xiamen City.

Legal Representative: Chen Jianling, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yuheng, lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

Agent ad litem: Bai Shaoxiang, lawyer of Fujian Tianheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xiamen Huanghe Technology Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 105, Building 7, Dayang Shanzhuang, Longhu Nan San Li, Siming District, Xiamen City.

Legal Representative: Wu Junchen, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhuang Ruiming, lawyer of Fujian Xiamen Mingjia Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wu Daxin, General Manager of Xiamen Huanghe Technology Trade Co., Ltd.

The appellant, Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dayang Company), and the appellee, Xiamen Huanghe Technology Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huanghe Company), were involved in a dispute over a patent implementation license contract. Dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2003) Min Zhi Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court, Dayang Company appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. The legal representatives of the appellant Dayang Company and the appellee Huanghe Company did not appear in court, but their respective agents ad litem appeared and participated in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The Fujian High People's Court found after trial that: On November 19, 1999, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. (Party A) and Dayang Company (Party B) entered into a "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract". The contract stipulated that Party B would implement Party A's patented technology project, which was a stone pressing and forming machine, with the machine brand being "Huanghe" brand NEW-668 type stone slab one-time pressing and forming machine. The scope of technology implementation license was that Party A licensed Party B to jointly implement the project with Party A within Fujian Province, and also licensed Party B to be the exclusive developer, producer, and seller of Party A's patented project and products in the Shanghai area and Japan. Party B could apply for patents in Japan and exclusively produce and sell. After signing the contract, Party B would send personnel to Party A's factory for technical training, with relevant costs borne by Party A. Within ten days after signing the contract, Party B would pay Party A a deposit of RMB 500,000. Within 100 days after receiving the deposit, Party A would be responsible for manufacturing the production line to be supplied to Party B under the contract in batches and delivering it to the factory designated by Party B. RMB 300,000 would be paid before the installation and commissioning of the machinery and equipment at Party B's location, and RMB 200,000 would be paid after the installation and commissioning passed inspection. In addition to the full payment of RMB 1,000,000 as specified in the preceding paragraph, the remaining RMB 4,000,000 would be paid by Party B using the real estate property located at Yangming Building, Jianye West Road, Hubin North Road, Xiamen City, valued at RMB 3,724,050. Party A agreed to accept this property as payment for the contract amount, but Party B was required to sign a purchase contract for the said units with Party A within two days after the signing of this contract and to complete the notarization and property right transfer procedures.

After the contract was signed, Dayang Company delivered the Yangming Building property to Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. as payment for the contract amount, but did not pay the deposit as stipulated in the contract.

On November 25, 1999, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. signed a "Consignment Processing Contract" with Quanzhou Fengze District Beifeng Hydraulic Machinery Factory, entrusting it to produce 50 Huanghe brand NEW-668A type stone slab one-time pressing and forming machines and 250 sets of Huanghe brand special molds, and paid the contract amount. On December 23, 1999, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. signed a "Product Manufacturing Agreement" with Xiamen Yangxing Xingye Conveyor Co., Ltd., ordering three heavy-duty suspension conveyors. When the hanging conveyor line was transported to Dayang Company's production base for installation, it was obstructed by Wang Guan, the project manager of Dayang Company, resulting in the inability to install the conveyor line. Later, upon notice from Dayang Company, Xiamen Yangxing Xingye Conveyor Co., Ltd. transported the conveyor line back. Because Dayang Company did not allow the installation of equipment, Wu Daxin, then legal representative of Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd., had to notify Quanzhou Fengze District Beifeng Hydraulic Machinery Factory to suspend production of the machines and molds. The signed patent technology cooperation and patent technology implementation license contract ceased to be performed.

On January 21, 2000, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. sent a letter to Dayang Company, stating that it had performed its relevant obligations under the contract and requiring Dayang Company to pay the deposit of RMB 500,000. On January 26, 2000, in response to the letter from Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd., Dayang Company replied, claiming that the other party's product did not have patent protection and that, due to factors such as the market price of each square meter of product from other suppliers being only RMB 25, it would be impossible for Dayang Company to achieve the purpose of the contract. Dayang Company requested Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. to propose a solution, otherwise it would apply to the court for revocation or modification of the contract in accordance with the Contract Law. On January 28, 2000, in response to Dayang Company's letter of January 26, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. again wrote to Dayang Company, refuting Dayang Company's grounds for terminating or modifying the contract. On March 1, 2000, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. again wrote to Dayang Company, demanding that Dayang Company immediately perform the contract signed by both parties. Thereafter, the parties did not have further contact or negotiations regarding the performance of the contract, and Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. did not apply to the court for revocation or modification of the contract in dispute.

The court of first instance held that the "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract" signed on November 19, 1999, between Dayang Company and Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. was a patent technology implementation license contract voluntarily entered into by both parties. The content of the contract did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, was a valid contract, and should be protected by law. After the contract was signed, although Dayang Company had partially performed its obligations under the contract by using the real estate property of Xiamen Yangming Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. to offset the contract amount, it failed to pay the deposit as stipulated in the contract and continued to fulfill the payment obligation, which constituted a breach of contract. Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd., after performing part of its obligations under the contract, was forced to cease further performance due to unreasonable obstruction by Dayang Company. Dayang Company's claim for rescission of the contract on the grounds that Huanghe Company had not performed the contract lacked factual basis. The contract in dispute did not meet the conditions for rescission of a contract as stipulated in the Contract Law of the PRC, nor did the "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract" signed by both parties specifically stipulate the conditions for rescission. Accordingly, given that Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. did not agree to rescind the contract, Dayang Company's unilateral request to rescind the contract and return the payments should not be supported. Although the parties had ceased performance of the contract for over three years by the time of filing this lawsuit, the Contract Law of the PRC does not stipulate that the request for rescission of a contract is subject to the statute of limitations. Therefore, Huanghe Company's defense that this lawsuit had exceeded the statute of limitations lacked legal basis and its argument was not adopted. However, its defense that Dayang Company's request for rescission was unreasonable and should be dismissed was supported. In summary, in accordance with Article 64, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 8 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the court ruled: The claim of the plaintiff, Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd., was dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 35,010 was borne by the plaintiff, Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd.

Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment of the Fujian High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract" in dispute in this case is invalid. The reasons are: (1) The contract violates mandatory provisions of law. The appellee's purpose in implementing the patent license was to force the sale of, and sell at a high price, equipment that was not essential for implementing the patent, which constitutes "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress." (2) The appellee, through fraudulent means, induced the appellant to make a false expression of intent and enter into a technology contract, which is an invalid civil act. The appellee was not the patentee but claimed to be, leading the appellant to make a mistaken expression of intent in signing the contract. 2. The judgment of the court of first instance was clearly unreasonable and inconsistent with the Contract Law. The parties had ceased performance of the contract for over three years, and the purpose of the contract, i.e., to implement the patented technology, had been lost. Requiring the parties to return to the state at the time of signing the contract and continue performance was clearly unreasonable. The contract should be rescinded. The appellant requested the second instance court to reverse the original judgment, order the appellee to return the property obtained under the contract to the appellant, and order the appellee to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The appellee, Huanghe Company, argued in response: 1. The appellant's claim that the contract in dispute was invalid for "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress" has no legal basis; the contract is lawful and valid. The purpose of the contract in dispute was the sale and license of use of the patented technology product. The equipment was an integral part of the contract. The stone pressing and forming machine was a machine containing the appellee's patented technology and was specialized equipment. For the appellant to use the appellee's patented technology, purchasing the machine was necessary. 2. The appellant's claim that the appellee induced the appellant to make a false expression of intent and enter into the contract through fraudulent means lacks factual basis. 3. The court of first instance correctly dismissed the appellant's claim for rescission of the contract on the grounds that the conditions for rescission under the Contract Law were not met. The appellant's argument that the purpose of the contract had been lost and the contract could not be performed is untenable. 4. The appellant's lawsuit at first instance had exceeded the statute of limitations, and its civil rights should not be protected. The appellee requested the second instance court to uphold the first-instance judgment.

During the second instance of this Court, after questioning the parties and exchanging evidence before the hearing, the following issues in dispute between the parties were identified: 1. Does the contract in dispute fall within the circumstance of "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress" as stipulated in Article 329 of the Contract Law of the PRC, and is the patent implementation license contract therefore invalid? 2. Is the contract invalid due to fraud by the appellee, Huanghe Company? 3. Does Article 110, item (3), of the Contract Law of the PRC apply to the rescission of this contract? 4. Did the appellee, Huanghe Company, fully perform its obligations under the contract?

This Court, upon trial, found that the facts found by the court of first instance were true, and the agents ad litem of both parties did not dispute the facts found by the court of first instance.

This Court additionally found the following regarding the change of name of Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd.: On November 2, 1994, Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. was established. On February 19, 2001, with the approval of the Xiamen Administration for Industry and Commerce, its enterprise name was changed to Xiamen Huanghe Technology Trade Co., Ltd., with a business term from November 2, 1994, to November 2, 2009.

This Court also found that when the appellant, Dayang Company, filed the lawsuit at first instance, it claimed that Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd. had failed to perform its contractual obligations and requested rescission of the "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract" signed between them and an order for the return of property obtained under the contract. At the first-instance hearing, the agent ad litem of Dayang Company requested to change the claim to a declaration that the "Patent Technology Cooperation and Patent Technology Implementation License Contract" signed by both parties was invalid. The court of first instance did not allow Dayang Company to change the claim on the grounds that the change exceeded the time limit for submitting evidence.

This Court holds: Based on the facts already found, the appellee, Huanghe Company, has performed most of its obligations under the contract signed by both parties. The part not yet performed was due to obstruction by the appellant, Dayang Company. The appellant, Dayang Company's failure to pay the deposit of RMB 500,000 and other actions breached the contract and caused the patent implementation license contract in question not to be fully performed. For this, the appellant, Dayang Company, should bear liability for breach of contract.

At first instance, the appellant, Dayang Company, first claimed rescission of the patent implementation license contract, and later, after the deadline, sought to change the claim to a declaration of invalidity of the contract, which was not permitted by the court of first instance. At second instance, the appellant, Dayang Company, again sought a declaration of invalidity of the contract on the grounds of illegal monopolization of technology and hindrance of technological progress. This claim was not within the scope of the claim originally brought by the appellant, Dayang Company. However, given that the appellee, Huanghe Company, made a substantive defense in the second instance regarding the grounds raised by the appellant, Dayang Company, for the invalidity of the patent implementation license contract and agreed to treat this as an issue in dispute, the second instance court conducted a court investigation on this issue during the trial, and both parties presented their oral arguments.

Pursuant to Article 329 of the Contract Law of the PRC, an act of "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress" refers to requiring the technology recipient to accept ancillary conditions that are not essential for implementing the technology, including purchasing technology, services, raw materials, equipment, or products that the technology recipient does not need, accepting personnel that the technology recipient does not need, and unreasonably restricting the technology recipient's freedom to choose sources for purchasing raw materials, parts, or equipment. The stone forming machine involved in the disputed patent implementation license contract in this case is specialized equipment containing the patented technology. For the appellant to implement the technology, purchasing the machine equipment was necessary. Pursuant to the terms of the patent implementation license contract, the equipment used for implementing the patented technology included the main machine, special molds, and conveyor belts, to establish a production line with a cost of RMB 5,000,000. The patent implementation license that the appellant, Dayang Company, obtained from the appellee, Huanghe Company, was not for manufacturing the patented product (i.e., the stone pressing and forming machine) but for producing and selling the final product, stone, by using the patented product. Therefore, stipulating in the patent implementation license contract that the technology licensor would provide the specialized equipment necessary for performing the contract does not violate the provisions of laws or regulations. The appellant, Dayang Company, claimed that this equipment was imposed on it by the appellee but did not provide evidence to support its claim. Therefore, its ground for appeal seeking to confirm the invalidity of the contract on the basis of "illegally monopolizing technology or hindering technological progress" cannot stand.

Article 3 of the disputed patent implementation license contract in this case specifies the application date, patent application number, patent number, patent validity period, patent certificate number, and other true information related to the patent technology. At the time of signing the contract, the legal representative of the appellee, Huanghe Company (its predecessor being Xiamen Huanghe Trade Co., Ltd.), Wu Daxin, was the patentee of the utility model patent for the stone pressing and forming machine. Huanghe Company, as the licensor under the disputed contract in this case, did not engage in any infringing act without the permission of the patentee. Its then legal representative was also the patentee who signed the contract as the licensor. The rights and obligations stipulated in the contract did not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the patentee or others. Therefore, the argument that the contract was entered into due to fraud by the appellee is untenable. As the licensee under a patent implementation license contract, where the contract already contains information related to the patent, the licensee has an obligation to verify the truthfulness of the contract content to avoid unnecessary commercial risks. Based on the existing evidence, the patent implementation license contract in question was a true expression of the intent of both parties, and its content did not violate national laws or regulations. It should be recognized as a valid contract. The appellant, Dayang Company's ground for appeal that the contract was invalid due to fraud by the appellee, Huanghe Company, cannot stand.

When the appellant, Dayang Company, filed the lawsuit at first instance, its claim was solely for rescission of the patent implementation license contract. The appellee, Huanghe Company, did not seek to pursue liability for breach of contract against the other party. The court of first instance, based on the validity and performance of the contract, Dayang Company's breach, and the claims of the parties, correctly dismissed Dayang Company's claim. This Court considers that the utility model patent for the stone slab one-time pressing and forming machine involved in this case remains valid, the appellant, Dayang Company, has paid most of the contract amount, and the licensor, Huanghe Company, has performed its obligation to provide the equipment stipulated in the contract. As long as both parties act in good faith and uphold the principle of honoring contracts, engage in equal negotiation, and make efforts, the purpose of the contract can still be achieved. Even if the parties decide to terminate the contract in the future, they should do so upon assuming corresponding responsibilities according to law and negotiate separately on a basis of equality regarding the aftermath.

In summary, the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1), of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 35,010 and the second-instance litigation fee of RMB 35,010, totaling RMB 70,020, shall be borne by the appellant, Xiamen Dayang Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang
Acting Judge: Duan Lihong
Acting Judge: Li Jian

June 16, 2004

Clerk: Cui Lina

【Profile of the Presiding Judge】

Wang Yongchang, Senior Judge: Born in 1956, Master of Laws, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2001.
